sources.supports: building/storey/space topology; zones, elements, interfaces, adjacency, containment, and geometry links

paper_takeaways: A space/zone has a 3D spatial extent and is distinct from a tangible building element.
A building can be decomposed as site -> building -> storey -> space.
Elements such as walls, doors and windows are contained in, adjacent to, or intersecting with zones.
Interfaces qualify relationships at boundaries, for example access between a space and corridor through a door.
Geometry and materials are assigned to zones/elements after their topology is described.
modeling_decision: Model one complete room zone first, then model its boundary elements and interfaces. Exclude furniture so the test isolates architectural hard finish.
